name: 240-bottom-placement-negates-the-land-angle
why: A land with a turn OF ITS OWN on a flipped part. U4 sits at (10,10) unturned on the BOTTOM; the land is at the component origin, 2.0 x 0.6, turned 45 within the footprint. Reflecting the footprint reverses the sense of that turn, so the land's board angle is 0 - 45 = -45, and in this y-down frame a board angle of -45 points the long axis along (+x, +y): the unit direction is (0.7071, 0.7071). The probe sits 0.9 mm out along it, at (10.6364, 10.6364), which is 0.9 of the 1.0 mm half-length and dead on the centreline - inside. Leave the angle at +45 and the long axis points along (+x, -y) instead; the same probe is then 0.9 mm off the centreline of a land whose half-width is 0.3, so it misses by 0.6 mm and its 0.125 mm cap does not close that. 090/100 pin the 45-degree land itself on the front; this is the case that fails if only the POSITION is mirrored and the angle is left alone.
